PHBR2 p.107. NOT PURCHASABLE and not carried: this bolt is CREATED BY THE CROSSBOW OF ANGLING on command, up to three times per day. It exists as a record because the +2 belongs to the BOLT, not to the bow -- the crossbow itself is an ordinary light crossbow and carries no bonus. Counts as a +2 bolt for attack rolls and damage where applicable. When fired it trails a pencil-thin snaking line of faint blue light (which radiates magic fairly strongly) connecting it to the crossbow. On impact the head expands into a small claw which embeds itself in the target so the bolt grips strongly; a second command word 'reels in' the target, the cord shrinking to drag it to the archer at up to 60 feet per round depending on weight and friction. If the target is heavier than the archer, or immovable or braced, THE CROSSBOWMAN MAY BE DRAGGED TO THE TARGET instead -- which can be exploited to pull oneself up to a ceiling or a wall. The magical cord is AC -2 and takes 15 points of damage to destroy; nonmagical weapons do it no damage.

PHBR2 p.96. A broad, flat head with backward-facing barbs, designed to grip when shot into wooden surfaces. Used to carry a rope to a wall, battlement or similar structure at greater range than a thrown grappling iron. TABLE 30 (p.96): +15 for Tree Branches and Wooden Walls. TWO METHODS (p.96). ONE-ROPE: the rope is tied straight to the arrow and the thief climbs it directly. Simple, but the rope must bear his weight, which HALVES ALL BOW RANGES, applies -5 to the Table 30 modifier below, and carries -2 TO HIT AND DAMAGE IF THE ARROW IS USED IN COMBAT FOR ANY REASON. TWO-ROPE: a light string runs through a loop on the arrow and is used to pull a stout rope through after the arrow lands. The string is light enough not to affect the arrow's flight, so NONE of those penalties apply -- but it takes one round per 20 feet of rope played out, and twice the rope, since it runs out and back. Table 29 base chances (p.95), rolled on d100 as Miss / Catch-and-Slip / Catch: Stone Parapet 01-72 / 73-78 / 79-00; Stone Wall Top 01-83 / 84-89 / 90-00; Tree Branches 01-66 / 67-70 / 71-00; Rocky Ledge 01-88 / 89-93 / 94-00; Wooden Wall 01-70 / 71-74 / 75-00. A catch-and-slip holds, then works free after 1d6 rounds of bearing weight; thieves should test a grapple by pulling on it for six rounds first.

PHBR2 p.96. The head looks like a fairly long arrowhead of normal width until fired: the rope is fixed at the thief's end, and when the arrow reaches the rope's limit the sudden tension opens the head into a three-pointed grappling hook 6 to 8 inches across, the equal of most ordinary grappling irons. Better aerodynamics and a better chance of gripping than the minor grapple, but a considerably reduced range. CAN ONLY BE USED WITH THE ONE-ROPE METHOD because of how it works, so its halved ranges and -2 to hit and damage are NOT conditional -- they always apply.
